1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Zero-token, fail-closed merge-tail patrol.  It is the only actor that merges
3	# merge-when-green PRs; every decision is tied to the currently observed SHA.
4	set -uo pipefail
5	
6	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
7	STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/pr-babysit"
8	mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
9	LOG="$STATE_DIR/patrol.log"
10	LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"
11	PREFLIGHT="${PR_BABYSIT_PREFLIGHT:-$ROOT/bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh}"
12	exec 9>"$LOCK"
13	flock -n 9 || exit 0
14	log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }
15	
16	# Returns non-zero if the durable control-plane record could not be written.
17	transition() {
18	  local bead="$1" metadata="$2" notes="$3" key="$4" message="$5" previous
19	  previous="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_last_transition // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
20	  [[ "$previous" == "$key" ]] && return 0
21	  [[ -z "$previous" && "$notes" == *"transition=$key"* ]] && return 0
22	  bd update "$bead" --set-metadata "pr_babysit_last_transition=$key" \
23	    --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] transition=$key — $message" >/dev/null 2>&1
24	}
25	
26	# Keep the merge-when-green label if any prerequisite mutation fails; the next
27	# patrol can safely retry.  Do not claim a bead is blocked unless all mutations
28	# completed.
29	block() {
30	  local bead="$1" metadata="$2" notes="$3" key="$4" message="$5"
31	  local previous args=()
32	  previous="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_last_transition // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
33	  args=(update "$bead" --status open --assignee "" --remove-label merge-when-green --add-label merge-blocked)
34	  if [[ "$previous" != "$key" && ! ( -z "$previous" && "$notes" == *"transition=$key"* ) ]]; then
35	    args+=(--set-metadata "pr_babysit_last_transition=$key" --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] transition=$key — $message")
36	  fi
37	  if ! bd "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then log "$bead: block deferred (atomic update failed)"; return 1; fi
38	  log "$bead: BLOCKED ($message)"
39	}
40	
41	legacy_policy() {
42	  # Only a complete, latest handoff line is authoritative; prose elsewhere is
43	  # not policy. Output method<TAB>rerun or nothing.
44	  sed -nE 's/^\[pr-handoff [^]]+\] repo=([^ ]+) pr=([1-9][0-9]*) method=(squash|merge|rebase) flake_rerun=(allowed|no) .*/\1\t\2\t\3\t\4/p' <<<"$1" | tail -n1
45	}
46	
47	valid_repo_pr() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ && "$2" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; }
48	
49	cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
50	QUEUE="$(bd list --label merge-when-green --json 2>/dev/null)" || { log "bd unavailable; skipping"; exit 0; }
51	if ! jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"$QUEUE"; then log "bd returned malformed queue data"; exit 0; fi
52	
53	while read -r item; do
54	  bead="$(jq -r '.id // empty' <<<"$item")"; ref="$(jq -r '.external_ref // empty' <<<"$item")"; notes="$(jq -r '.notes // empty' <<<"$item")"
55	  [[ -n "$bead" ]] || { log "queue item has no id"; continue; }
56	  metadata_raw="$(jq -c 'if (.metadata? == null) then {} else .metadata end' <<<"$item")"
57	  if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"$metadata_raw"; then
58	    block "$bead" '{}' "$notes" "metadata-malformed" "Bead metadata is not an object; needs agent judgment."
59	    continue
60	  fi
61	  metadata="$metadata_raw"
62	  legacy="$(legacy_policy "$notes")"
63	  legacy_repo="$(cut -f1 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_pr="$(cut -f2 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_method="$(cut -f3 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_rerun="$(cut -f4 <<<"$legacy")"
64	
65	  repo=""; pr=""
66	  if [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh:([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)#([1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
67	    repo="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; pr="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
68	  elif [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh-pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
69	    repo="gastownhall/beads"; pr="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
70	  elif [[ -z "$ref" ]]; then
71	    repo="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_repo // empty' <<<"$metadata")"; pr="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_pr // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
72	    if ! valid_repo_pr "$repo" "$pr"; then repo="$legacy_repo"; pr="$legacy_pr"; fi
73	    if ! valid_repo_pr "$repo" "$pr"; then
74	      block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "missing-reference" "No valid external_ref or metadata PR identity; needs agent judgment."
75	      continue
76	    fi
77	  else
78	    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "reference-malformed" "Unparseable external_ref; needs agent judgment."
79	    continue
80	  fi
81	  meta_repo="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_repo // empty' <<<"$metadata")"; meta_pr="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_pr // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
82	  if { [[ -n "$meta_repo" || -n "$meta_pr" ]]; } && { [[ "$meta_repo" != "$repo" || "$meta_pr" != "$pr" ]]; }; then

89	  fi
90	
91	  # Present metadata must be valid. Only absent/null keys may fall back to the
92	  # latest exact legacy handoff marker.
93	  method_present="$(jq 'has("pr_babysit_method") and .pr_babysit_method != null' <<<"$metadata")"
94	  rerun_present="$(jq 'has("pr_babysit_flake_rerun") and .pr_babysit_flake_rerun != null' <<<"$metadata")"

96	  if [[ "$method_present" == true && ! "$method" =~ ^(squash|merge|rebase)$ ]] || [[ "$rerun_present" == true && ! "$rerun_policy" =~ ^(allowed|no)$ ]]; then
97	    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "policy-malformed" "pr_babysit policy metadata is invalid; needs agent judgment."
98	    continue
99	  fi
100	  [[ "$method_present" == true ]] || method="$legacy_method"
101	  [[ "$rerun_present" == true ]] || rerun_policy="$legacy_rerun"
102	  if [[ ! "$method" =~ ^(squash|merge|rebase)$ || ! "$rerun_policy" =~ ^(allowed|no)$ ]]; then
103	    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "policy-unavailable" "No valid handoff policy exists; needs agent judgment."
104	    continue

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Zero-token, fail-closed merge-tail patrol.  It is the only actor that merges
# merge-when-green PRs; every decision is tied to the currently observed SHA.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/pr-babysit"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
LOG="$STATE_DIR/patrol.log"
LOCK="$STATE_DIR/lock"
PREFLIGHT="${PR_BABYSIT_PREFLIGHT:-$ROOT/bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh}"
exec 9>"$LOCK"
flock -n 9 || exit 0
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >>"$LOG"; }

# Returns non-zero if the durable control-plane record could not be written.
transition() {
  local bead="$1" metadata="$2" notes="$3" key="$4" message="$5" previous
  previous="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_last_transition // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
  [[ "$previous" == "$key" ]] && return 0
  [[ -z "$previous" && "$notes" == *"transition=$key"* ]] && return 0
  bd update "$bead" --set-metadata "pr_babysit_last_transition=$key" \
    --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] transition=$key — $message" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# Keep the merge-when-green label if any prerequisite mutation fails; the next
# patrol can safely retry.  Do not claim a bead is blocked unless all mutations
# completed.
block() {
  local bead="$1" metadata="$2" notes="$3" key="$4" message="$5"
  local previous args=()
  previous="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_last_transition // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
  args=(update "$bead" --status open --assignee "" --remove-label merge-when-green --add-label merge-blocked)
  if [[ "$previous" != "$key" && ! ( -z "$previous" && "$notes" == *"transition=$key"* ) ]]; then
    args+=(--set-metadata "pr_babysit_last_transition=$key" --append-notes "[pr-babysit $(date -u +%FT%TZ)] transition=$key — $message")
  fi
  if ! bd "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then log "$bead: block deferred (atomic update failed)"; return 1; fi
  log "$bead: BLOCKED ($message)"
}

legacy_policy() {
  # Only a complete, latest handoff line is authoritative; prose elsewhere is
  # not policy. Output method<TAB>rerun or nothing.
  sed -nE 's/^\[pr-handoff [^]]+\] repo=([^ ]+) pr=([1-9][0-9]*) method=(squash|merge|rebase) flake_rerun=(allowed|no) .*/\1\t\2\t\3\t\4/p' <<<"$1" | tail -n1
}

valid_repo_pr() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ && "$2" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; }

cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
QUEUE="$(bd list --label merge-when-green --json 2>/dev/null)" || { log "bd unavailable; skipping"; exit 0; }
if ! jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"$QUEUE"; then log "bd returned malformed queue data"; exit 0; fi

while read -r item; do
  bead="$(jq -r '.id // empty' <<<"$item")"; ref="$(jq -r '.external_ref // empty' <<<"$item")"; notes="$(jq -r '.notes // empty' <<<"$item")"
  [[ -n "$bead" ]] || { log "queue item has no id"; continue; }
  metadata_raw="$(jq -c 'if (.metadata? == null) then {} else .metadata end' <<<"$item")"
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"$metadata_raw"; then
    block "$bead" '{}' "$notes" "metadata-malformed" "Bead metadata is not an object; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi
  metadata="$metadata_raw"
  legacy="$(legacy_policy "$notes")"
  legacy_repo="$(cut -f1 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_pr="$(cut -f2 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_method="$(cut -f3 <<<"$legacy")"; legacy_rerun="$(cut -f4 <<<"$legacy")"

  repo=""; pr=""
  if [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh:([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)#([1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
    repo="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; pr="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
  elif [[ "$ref" =~ ^gh-pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
    repo="gastownhall/beads"; pr="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  elif [[ -z "$ref" ]]; then
    repo="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_repo // empty' <<<"$metadata")"; pr="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_pr // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
    if ! valid_repo_pr "$repo" "$pr"; then repo="$legacy_repo"; pr="$legacy_pr"; fi
    if ! valid_repo_pr "$repo" "$pr"; then
      block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "missing-reference" "No valid external_ref or metadata PR identity; needs agent judgment."
      continue
    fi
  else
    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "reference-malformed" "Unparseable external_ref; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi
  meta_repo="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_repo // empty' <<<"$metadata")"; meta_pr="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_pr // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
  if { [[ -n "$meta_repo" || -n "$meta_pr" ]]; } && { [[ "$meta_repo" != "$repo" || "$meta_pr" != "$pr" ]]; }; then
    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "reference-metadata-mismatch" "external_ref and pr_babysit metadata disagree; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi
  if [[ -n "$legacy" ]] && { [[ "$legacy_repo" != "$repo" || "$legacy_pr" != "$pr" ]]; }; then
    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "reference-legacy-mismatch" "external_ref and legacy handoff identity disagree; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi

  # Present metadata must be valid. Only absent/null keys may fall back to the
  # latest exact legacy handoff marker.
  method_present="$(jq 'has("pr_babysit_method") and .pr_babysit_method != null' <<<"$metadata")"
  rerun_present="$(jq 'has("pr_babysit_flake_rerun") and .pr_babysit_flake_rerun != null' <<<"$metadata")"
  method="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_method // empty' <<<"$metadata")"; rerun_policy="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_flake_rerun // empty' <<<"$metadata")"

    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "policy-malformed" "pr_babysit policy metadata is invalid; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi
  [[ "$method_present" == true ]] || method="$legacy_method"
  [[ "$rerun_present" == true ]] || rerun_policy="$legacy_rerun"
  if [[ ! "$method" =~ ^(squash|merge|rebase)$ || ! "$rerun_policy" =~ ^(allowed|no)$ ]]; then
    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "policy-unavailable" "No valid handoff policy exists; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi

  if ! pr_json="$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json state,headRefOid 2>>"$LOG")"; then
    transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "pr-data-unavailable" "GitHub PR command failed; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    continue
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" and (.state | type == "string") and (.headRefOid | type == "string")' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"$pr_json"; then
    transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "pr-data-malformed" "GitHub PR data was malformed; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    continue
  fi
  state="$(jq -r .state <<<"$pr_json")"; head="$(jq -r .headRefOid <<<"$pr_json")"
  if [[ "$state" == MERGED ]]; then
    if bd close "$bead" --reason "PR $repo#$pr merged (observed by pr-babysit)." >/dev/null 2>&1; then log "$bead: $repo#$pr already merged; bead closed"; else log "$bead: close failed"; fi
    continue
  fi
  if [[ "$state" == CLOSED ]]; then
    if transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "closed-unmerged" "PR closed unmerged upstream; needs a decision." && bd update "$bead" --remove-label merge-when-green >/dev/null 2>&1; then log "$bead: $repo#$pr closed unmerged; label removed"; else log "$bead: closed-unmerged mutation failed"; fi
    continue
  fi
  if [[ "$state" != OPEN || ! "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,64}$ ]]; then
    transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "pr-state-or-head-invalid" "GitHub returned an unsafe PR state or head; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    continue
  fi

  if ! checks="$(gh pr checks "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json name,bucket,link 2>>"$LOG")" || ! jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; type == "object" and (.name | type == "string") and (.bucket | type == "string") and (.bucket == "pass" or .bucket == "pending" or .bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "skipping" or .bucket == "cancel"))' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"${checks:-}"; then
    transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "checks-unavailable:$head" "GitHub checks data was unavailable, empty, malformed, or unknown; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    continue
  fi
  pending="$(jq '[.[] | select(.bucket == "pending")] | length' <<<"$checks")"; failing="$(jq '[.[] | select(.bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "cancel")] | length' <<<"$checks")"
  if (( pending > 0 )); then transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "waiting:$head:$pending:$failing" "Checks pending; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"; continue; fi

  if (( failing > 0 )); then
    rerun_head="$(jq -r '.pr_babysit_rerun_head // empty' <<<"$metadata")"
    legacy_spent=0; [[ "$notes" == *"flake-rerun-done"* ]] && legacy_spent=1
    if [[ "$rerun_policy" == allowed && "$rerun_head" != "$head" && "$legacy_spent" == 0 ]]; then
      runs="$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "cancel") | (.link // "") | capture("/runs/(?<id>[0-9]+)")?.id // empty' <<<"$checks" | sort -u)"
      if [[ -z "$runs" ]]; then block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "checks-no-rerun-target:$head" "Failing checks have no rerunnable run; needs agent judgment."; continue; fi

      if ! bd update "$bead" --set-metadata "pr_babysit_rerun_head=$head" >/dev/null 2>&1; then log "$bead: rerun deferred (reservation failed)"; continue; fi
      rerun_ok=0
      while read -r run_id; do [[ -n "$run_id" ]] && gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed >>"$LOG" 2>&1 && rerun_ok=1; done <<<"$runs"
      if (( rerun_ok )); then transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "rerun:$head" "Reran failed checks; waiting for this head." || log "$bead: rerun transition failed"; else block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "rerun-failed:$head" "Rerun command failed; needs agent judgment."; fi
      continue
    fi
    block "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "checks-persistent:$head" "Checks still fail after rerun budget; needs agent judgment."
    continue
  fi

  preflight_out="$(PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1 "$PREFLIGHT" "$pr" --repo "$repo" 2>&1)"; preflight_status=$?
  [[ -n "$preflight_out" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$preflight_out" >>"$LOG"

    elif [[ -n "$blocks" ]]; then
      transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "preflight-red-base:$head" "Base branch CI is red; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    else
      transition "$bead" "$metadata" "$notes" "preflight-unavailable:$head" "Preflight failed without a recognizable block; retained under patrol." || log "$bead: transition failed"
    fi

[0].metadata == $queued.metadata)' >/dev/null 2>/dev/null <<<"${current_issue:-}"; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hermetic behavioural tests for pr-babysit and pr-handoff.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
FAKE_BIN="$TMP/bin"
mkdir -p "$FAKE_BIN"

cat >"$FAKE_BIN/gh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$FAKE_GH_LOG"
case "${1:-} ${2:-}" in
  "pr view")
    if [[ -n "${FAKE_PR_BODY:-}" ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$FAKE_PR_BODY"; exit "${FAKE_PR_EXIT:-0}"; fi
    state="${FAKE_PR_STATE:-OPEN}"
    head="${FAKE_HEAD:-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa}"
    [[ -f "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_MARK:-/dev/null}" ]] && head="${FAKE_HEAD_AFTER_PREFLIGHT:-$head}"
    [[ -f "$FAKE_MERGE_MARK" ]] && state="${FAKE_POST_MERGE_STATE:-MERGED}"
    rollup="${FAKE_ROLLUP:-}"
    [[ -n "$rollup" ]] || rollup='[{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"SUCCESS"}]'
    jq -cn --arg state "$state" --arg head "$head" --argjson rollup "$rollup" '{title:"Example PR", state:$state, headRefOid:$head, statusCheckRollup:$rollup}'
    [[ -f "$FAKE_MERGE_MARK" ]] && exit "${FAKE_POST_PR_EXIT:-0}"
    exit "${FAKE_PR_EXIT:-0}"
    ;;
  "pr checks") printf '%s\n' "${FAKE_CHECKS:-[]}"; exit "${FAKE_CHECKS_EXIT:-0}" ;;
  "pr merge")
    [[ "${FAKE_MERGE_EXIT:-0}" == 0 ]] || exit "$FAKE_MERGE_EXIT"
    expected=""; for arg in "$@"; do [[ "$arg" == "--match-head-commit" ]] && next=1 && continue; [[ "${next:-}" == 1 ]] && expected="$arg" && unset next; done
    actual="${FAKE_HEAD:-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa}"; [[ -f "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_MARK:-/dev/null}" ]] && actual="${FAKE_HEAD_AFTER_PREFLIGHT:-$actual}"
    [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]] || exit 65
    touch "$FAKE_MERGE_MARK"
    ;;
  "run rerun") exit "${FAKE_RERUN_EXIT:-0}" ;;
  *) echo "unexpected gh invocation: $*" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac
EOF
cat >"$FAKE_BIN/bd" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$FAKE_BD_LOG"
[[ -z "${FAKE_BD_FAIL_ON:-}" || "${1:-}" != "$FAKE_BD_FAIL_ON" ]] || exit 1
[[ -z "${FAKE_BD_FAIL_MATCH:-}" || " $* " != *"$FAKE_BD_FAIL_MATCH"* ]] || exit 1
case "${1:-}" in
  list)
    if [[ " $* " == *" --label "* ]]; then
      cat "$FAKE_QUEUE"
    else
      ref=""; for arg in "$@"; do [[ "${next:-}" == 1 ]] && ref="$arg" && unset next; [[ "$arg" == "--external-ref" ]] && next=1; done
      jq --arg ref "$ref" '[.[] | select(.external_ref == $ref)]' "$FAKE_QUEUE"
    fi
    ;;
  show) jq --arg id "$2" '[.[] | select(.id == $id)]' "$FAKE_QUEUE" ;;
  create) printf '{"id":"mybd-created"}\n' ;;
  update)
    bead="$2"; shift 2
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
      case "$1" in
        --set-metadata)
          pair="$2"; key="${pair%%=*}"; value="${pair#*=}"
          qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"
          jq --arg id "$bead" --arg key "$key" --arg value "$value" \
            'map(if .id == $id then .metadata = ((.metadata // {}) + {($key): $value}) else . end)' \
            "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"
          mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"
          shift 2 ;;
        --external-ref)
          ref="$2"; qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"
          jq --arg id "$bead" --arg ref "$ref" 'map(if .id == $id then .external_ref = $ref else . end)' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"
          mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"; shift 2 ;;
        --status)
          value="$2"; qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"; jq --arg id "$bead" --arg value "$value" 'map(if .id == $id then .status = $value else . end)' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"; mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"; shift 2 ;;
        --assignee)
          value="$2"; qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"; jq --arg id "$bead" --arg value "$value" 'map(if .id == $id then .assignee = $value else . end)' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"; mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"; shift 2 ;;
        --remove-label)
          value="$2"; qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"; jq --arg id "$bead" --arg value "$value" 'map(if .id == $id then .labels = ((.labels // []) - [$value]) else . end)' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"; mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"; shift 2 ;;
        --add-label)
          value="$2"; qtmp="$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp"; jq --arg id "$bead" --arg value "$value" 'map(if .id == $id then .labels = (((.labels // []) + [$value]) | unique) else . end)' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$qtmp"; mv -f "$qtmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"; shift 2 ;;
        --append-notes) shift 2 ;;
        *) shift ;;
      esac
    done
    ;;
  close|unclaim) ;;
  *) echo "unexpected bd invocation: $*" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac
EOF
cat >"$FAKE_BIN/preflight" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
touch "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_MARK:-/dev/null}"
if [[ "${FAKE_REVOKE_LABEL:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
  jq 'map(.labels = ((.labels // []) - ["merge-when-green"]))' "$FAKE_QUEUE" >"$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp" && mv -f "$FAKE_QUEUE.tmp" "$FAKE_QUEUE"
fi
[[ -n "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT:-}" ]] || printf '%s\n' '[pass] Base branch main CI is green (required checks passed)'
[[ -z "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT:-}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$FAKE_PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT"
exit "${FAKE_PREFLIGHT_EXIT:-0}"
EOF
cat >"$FAKE_BIN/systemctl" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
EOF
cat >"$FAKE_BIN/systemd-analyze" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$FAKE_SYSTEMD_ANALYZE_LOG"
exit "${FAKE_SYSTEMD_ANALYZE_EXIT:-0}"
EOF
chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/gh" "$FAKE_BIN/bd" "$FAKE_BIN/preflight" "$FAKE_BIN/systemctl" "$FAKE_BIN/systemd-analyze"

export PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$PATH"
export PR_BABYSIT_PREFLIGHT="$FAKE_BIN/preflight"

fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
count() { grep -c -- "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || true; }

reset() {
  local name="$1" metadata="${2-}" notes="${3:-}" ref
  if [[ $# -ge 4 ]]; then ref="$4"; else ref="gh:gastownhall/beads#123"; fi
  [[ -n "$metadata" ]] || metadata='{}'
  CASE="$TMP/$name"; mkdir -p "$CASE"
  export FAKE_QUEUE="$CASE/queue.json" FAKE_BD_LOG="$CASE/bd.log" FAKE_GH_LOG="$CASE/gh.log" FAKE_MERGE_MARK="$CASE/merged" FAKE_PREFLIGHT_MARK="$CASE/preflight" FAKE_SYSTEMD_ANALYZE_LOG="$CASE/analyze.log"

  rm -f "$FAKE_PREFLIGHT_MARK"
  export FAKE_PR_STATE=OPEN FAKE_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa

    '[{id:"mybd-test", status:"in_progress", assignee:"maphew", labels:["merge-when-green"], external_ref:$ref, notes:$notes, metadata:$metadata}]' >"$FAKE_QUEUE"
  : >"$FAKE_BD_LOG"; : >"$FAKE_GH_LOG"
}

policy='{"pr_babysit_method":"squash","pr_babysit_flake_rerun":"allowed"}'

reset pending "$policy"
export FAKE_CHECKS='[{"name":"unit","bucket":"pending","link":""}]'
run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'pr merge' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 0 ]] || fail "pending checks merged"

reset rerun "$policy"
export FAKE_CHECKS='[{"name":"unit","bucket":"fail","link":"https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/42/job"}]'
run_patrol; run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'run rerun' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 1 ]] || fail "rerun was not limited to one per head"
[[ "$(jq -r '.[0].metadata.pr_babysit_rerun_head' "$FAKE_QUEUE")" == "$FAKE_HEAD" ]] || fail "successful rerun head was not recorded"

export FAKE_HEAD=cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
export FAKE_CHECKS='[{"name":"unit","bucket":"fail","link":"https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/43/job"}]'
run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'run rerun' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 1 ]] || fail "head change did not reset rerun budget"

export FAKE_HEAD=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd

run_patrol

[[ "$(count '^close ' "$FAKE_BD_LOG")" == 0 ]] || fail "open queued merge closed bead"
grep -q 'merge-queued:' "$FAKE_BD_LOG" || fail "queued merge was not transitioned"

run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'pr merge' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 0 ]] || fail "malformed PR data merged"

export FAKE_CHECKS='not json' FAKE_CHECKS_EXIT=1
run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'pr merge' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 0 ]] || fail "unavailable checks merged"

export FAKE_CHECKS='not json'
run_patrol
[[ "$(count 'pr merge' "$FAKE_GH_LOG")" == 0 ]] || fail "malformed checks merged"

# Review: pr-babysit merge-tail patrol series (mybd main, `d5d4355` → `1e33d26`)

## Overview

This series landed as five direct commits on main (no PR): the initial patrol (`d5d4355`, Fable), then four hardening rounds signed `codex-gpt-5.6-terra-high`. Net result:

- **`scripts/pr-babysit`** — a zero-token systemd-timer patrol that owns "merge when green" PR tails: reads `merge-when-green` beads, validates PR identity and policy, waits on pending checks, spends a one-per-head flake-rerun budget, runs a blocking `pr-preflight` base-health check, then merges with `--match-head-commit` CAS and closes the bead only after confirming `MERGED`.
- **`scripts/pr-handoff`** — session-side handoff: finds/creates the bead, writes namespaced `pr_babysit_*` metadata, labels it, warns if the timer isn't active.
- **`scripts/install-pr-babysit`** + systemd units — installer that resolves the stable checkout (worktree-aware via `--git-common-dir`), validates the path for systemd-unsafe characters, and verifies the generated unit.
- **`scripts/test-pr-babysit`** — ~35 hermetic behavioral tests with fake `gh`/`bd`/preflight.
- AGENTS.md documents the role split (sessions produce, only the patrol merges) motivated by the beads#4942 red-nix collision.

## What I verified empirically

- **Test suite passes** on this machine.
- **`gh pr checks --json` exits 0 even with failing checks** (tested against gastownhall/beads#4929, which has 2 failing checks). This was my top suspicion — the fake `gh` defaults `FAKE_CHECKS_EXIT=0`, and without `--json` the real command exits non-zero on fail/pending, which would have dead-ended the rerun/block paths at the `checks-unavailable` transition. Reality matches the fake; **no bug**.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array** with `.[0]` shape as the patrol assumes; `bd list --label merge-when-green --json` returns a clean array.
- The jq run-id capture expression (`capture(...)?.id // empty`, `pr-babysit:140`) parses and extracts correctly, including for empty links.

## Strengths

This is unusually careful bash for an auto-merge bot. The safety ladder is genuinely fail-closed at every rung: malformed queue data, malformed metadata, identity mismatches (external_ref vs metadata vs legacy note), invalid policy, gh non-zero status *even with valid JSON*, unknown check buckets, empty check lists, preflight exit-zero-without-explicit-green, head drift between checks and merge, merge-queued-but-not-merged, and bead-authorization revocation re-read immediately before the merge (`pr-babysit:178`). The rerun budget is reserved *before* calling GitHub so a crash conservatively spends it (`pr-babysit:142-144`). Transitions are idempotent across timer firings so bead notes don't grow unboundedly. The distinction between `transition` (retain under patrol, retry forever) and `block` (unclaim + relabel for agent judgment) is applied thoughtfully — notably red-base retains while other preflight blocks escalate.

## Findings

None are merge-blocking; the design bias is conservative throughout, so the failure modes below are livelocks or noise, not bad merges.

**1. Silent livelock on the pre-merge authorization CAS — `scripts/pr-babysit:178-181` (low-medium, observability).**
The CAS requires `bd show` output to deep-equal the queue snapshot (`status`, `assignee`, `external_ref`, `notes`, `metadata`). If `bd list` and `bd show` ever serialize a field differently (e.g. one omits an empty `assignee`, the other emits `""` — I confirmed `bd show` *omits* absent fields), every merge attempt skips with only a local `log` line. Unlike every other retained state, this path writes **no transition to the bead**, so a persistent mismatch is invisible to agents running `bd ready` — the bead just sits green and unmerged forever, and only `patrol.log` knows why. Suggest: after N consecutive CAS skips for the same head, write a `transition` (or at least log a distinctive escalating marker) so the failure surfaces on the bead.

**2. Note growth for long-pending PRs — `scripts/pr-babysit:134`.**
The `waiting:$head:$pending:$failing` key embeds live counts, so a PR whose pending count ticks down 10→0 appends up to ~10 notes per head, and again per push. Idempotency only holds for an *unchanged* count. Cheap fix: drop `$pending:$failing` from the key (keep them in the message text).

**3. Stale comment — `scripts/pr-babysit:42-44`.**
`legacy_policy` says "Output method<TAB>rerun" but emits `repo<TAB>pr<TAB>method<TAB>rerun`. The callers use all four fields correctly; only the comment is wrong.

**4. Test-coverage gaps (minor).**
Untested paths: already-`MERGED` at first read closes the bead (`pr-babysit:116-119`); `CLOSED`-unmerged removes the label (`:120-123`); patrol-side resolution of the legacy `gh-pr-N` external_ref (`:68-69` — only the handoff side of legacy refs is tested); partial rerun success (some `gh run rerun` calls fail, one succeeds). Given how much this suite already covers, these are polish.

**5. `statusCheckRollup` truncation risk — `scripts/pr-babysit:172` (informational).**
GraphQL rollup fields can paginate on PRs with very many checks; beads#4929 has 71 and returned fully, so this is theoretical at current scale — and truncation would fail toward "not all green," i.e. conservative.

**6. Machine-specific PATH baked into the unit — `scripts/systemd/pr-babysit.service`.**
`/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` is hardcoded. Fine for a personal repo, but if the timer is ever installed on the Windows/other machines mentioned in AGENTS.md, `bd`/`gh` resolution silently degrades to "bd unavailable; skipping" — which at least fails closed and logs.

## Conventions & security

- Follows repo conventions: bash scripts, extensionless, agent-signed commits, AGENTS.md policy documented alongside the mechanism, `PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1` per the stop-the-line rule.
- Injection surface is well-guarded: `repo`/`pr`/`method`/`rerun` are all regex-validated before reaching `gh` argv (`pr-babysit:47,96,102`; `pr-handoff:35-38`); bead notes (agent-writable) are only pattern-matched, never executed; the installer rejects systemd-metacharacter paths and escapes the sed replacement.
- One deliberate and correct choice worth calling out: the *only* authority to merge is the conjunction of bead label + valid policy + green checks + green base + unchanged head — no prose is trusted (`legacy_policy` requires the exact machine-written marker line, and mismatched legacy identity blocks).

## Verdict

Solid merge. The one change I'd actually make is finding 1 (surface persistent CAS skips on the bead); 2 and 3 are trivial cleanups to batch with it. Nothing here needs a revert or urgent follow-up — the failure modes are all "doesn't merge and tells you quietly," never "merges wrongly."

- Dependency-aware: Track blockers and relationships between issues
- Git-friendly: Dolt-powered version control with native sync
- Agent-optimized: JSON output, ready work detection, discovered-from links
- Prevents duplicate tracking systems and confusion

### Quick Start

**Check for ready work:**

```bash
bd ready --json
```

**Create new issues:**

```bash
bd create "Issue title" --description="Detailed context" -t bug|feature|task -p 0-4 --json
bd create "Issue title" --description="What this issue is about" -p 1 --deps discovered-from:bd-123 --json
```

**Claim and update:**

```bash
bd update <id> --claim --json
bd update bd-42 --priority 1 --json
```

**Complete work:**

```bash
bd close bd-42 --reason "Completed" --json
```

### Issue Types

- `bug` - Something broken
- `feature` - New functionality
- `task` - Work item (tests, docs, refactoring)
- `epic` - Large feature with subtasks
- `chore` - Maintenance (dependencies, tooling)

### Priorities

- `0` - Critical (security, data loss, broken builds)
- `1` - High (major features, important bugs)
- `2` - Medium (default, nice-to-have)
- `3` - Low (polish, optimization)
- `4` - Backlog (future ideas)

### Workflow for AI Agents

1. **Check ready work**: `bd ready` shows unblocked issues
2. **Claim your task atomically**: `bd update <id> --claim`
3. **Work on it**: Implement, test, document
4. **Discover new work?** Create linked issue:
   - `bd create "Found bug" --description="Details about what was found" -p 1 --deps discovered-from:<parent-id>`
5. **Complete**: `bd close <id> --reason "Done"`

### Quality
- Use `--acceptance` and `--design` fields when creating issues
- Use `--validate` to check description completeness

### Lifecycle
- `bd defer <id>` / `bd supersede <id>` for issue management
- `bd stale` / `bd orphans` / `bd lint` for hygiene
- `bd human <id>` to flag for human decisions
- `bd formula list` / `bd mol pour <name>` for structured workflows

### Sync

bd stores issue history in Dolt:

- Each write auto-commits to Dolt history
- Use `bd dolt push`/`bd dolt pull` for remote sync
- Do not treat `.beads/issues.jsonl` as the sync protocol

**Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/core-concepts/sync-concepts.md for details and anti-patterns.

- ✅ Use bd for ALL task tracking
- ✅ Always use `--json` flag for programmatic use
- ✅ Link discovered work with `discovered-from` dependencies
- ✅ Check `bd ready` before asking "what should I work on?"
- ❌ Do NOT create markdown TODO lists
- ❌ Do NOT use external issue trackers
- ❌ Do NOT duplicate tracking systems

For more details, see README.md and https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md.

## Agent Context Profiles

The managed Beads block is task-tracking guidance, not permission to override repository, user, or orchestrator instructions.

- **Conservative (default)**: Use `bd` for task tracking. Do not run git commits, git pushes, or Dolt remote sync unless explicitly asked. At handoff, report changed files, validation, and suggested next commands.
- **Minimal**: Keep tool instruction files as pointers to `bd prime`; use the same conservative git policy unless active instructions say otherwise.
- **Team-maintainer**: Only when the repository explicitly opts in, agents may close beads, run quality gates, commit, and push as part of session close. A current "do not commit" or "do not push" instruction still wins.

## Session Completion

This protocol applies when ending a Beads implementation workflow. It is subordinate to explicit user, repository, and orchestrator instructions.

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create beads for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **Handle git/sync by active profile**:
   ```bash
   # Conservative/minimal/default: report status and proposed commands; wait for approval.
   git status

   # Team-maintainer opt-in only, unless current instructions forbid it:
   git pull --rebase
   bd dolt push
   git push
   git status
   ```
5. **Hand off** - Summarize changes, validation, issue status, and any blocked sync/commit/push step

**Critical rules:**
- Explicit user or orchestrator instructions override this Beads block.
- Do not commit or push without clear authority from the active profile or the current user request.
- If a required sync or push is blocked, stop and report the exact command and error.

# Agent Instructions

This project uses **bd** (beads) for issue tracking. Run `bd prime` for full workflow context.

## Conventions

"gh ..." : use gh cli to interact with GitHub
"gh {number} ..." : use gh cli on gastownhall/beads repo for issue or PR {number}
"bd ..." : use bd cli to interact with beads
"run issue triage" / "triage" : run the pinned procedure in
`.claude/commands/triage.md` (the `/triage` command) - do not improvise a
triage workflow. It never posts text upstream; publication goes through
`scripts/tri-submit`, which is human-gated (see `scripts/README.md`).

### Windows / Daily Housekeeping

On Windows, confirm the `bd` on `PATH` is the expected version before running
housekeeping or bead commands:

```powershell
Get-Command bd
bd --version
Get-Content .beads/.local_version
```

The repo-local source build is `bd-main\bd.exe`. If `bd --version` is older
than `.beads/.local_version` and `bd-main\bd.exe` has the expected version,
replace the stale PATH binary at `C:\Users\Matt\.local\bin\bd.exe` with the
repo-local binary, after confirming no `bd` process is running. Keep a backup
named for the old version.

Several repo scripts are Bash scripts. From PowerShell, run them through Git
Bash rather than invoking them directly:

```powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' scripts/check-beads-config
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' scripts/verify-status
```

PowerShell wrappers are also available beside the extensionless scripts. When
staying in PowerShell, prefer the `.ps1` entrypoint:

```powershell
scripts/check-beads-config.ps1
scripts/verify-status.ps1
```

Run embedded-Dolt `bd`/`dolt` commands serially in this repo. Parallel `bd`
commands can leave Git helper processes or embedded-Dolt locks behind.

Daily start routine:

```powershell
git pull --rebase
bd prime
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' scripts/check-beads-config
bd context --json
git -c safe.directory=A:/dev/mybd/bd-main -C bd-main fetch --all --prune
bd ready
bd list --status=in_progress
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' scripts/verify-status
```

If a newer `bd` refuses to auto-apply pending schema migrations on this
remote-backed database, do not override it casually. Do not run
`BD_ALLOW_REMOTE_MIGRATE=1` unless you are explicitly acting as the single
designated migrator. For ordinary housekeeping, record that schema-sensitive
commands are blocked by the migration gate and continue with read-only checks
that do not require migration. Commands such as `bd stats`, `bd blocked`,
`bd stale`, `bd orphans`, and `bd lint` are useful when schema-compatible, but
they are best-effort checks while the local database is behind the current
binary's schema.

If `bd list` unexpectedly appears empty in this coordination repo, do not
restore `.beads` blindly. Run `scripts/check-beads-config`; the live local
database is `.beads/embeddeddolt/mybd` (issue prefix `mybd-`, synced via the
Dolt remote to maphew/mybd), and stale config can point `bd` at the empty
`beads` bootstrap database.
For the narrow known drift case where `.beads/metadata.json` points at empty
`beads` while `mybd` is populated and has the expected remote, run
`scripts/check-beads-config --fix`. If both databases contain issues, export
both and reconcile manually before changing metadata. Use
`scripts/pre-commit-beads-config` in local commit hooks or CI to reject
accidental `.beads/metadata.json` changes away from `mybd`; intentional
database renames require `MYBD_ALLOW_DB_RENAME=1`.

When working on beads, spawn agents according to their metadata hints.
The checked-in Codex skill for those hints is `.codex/skills/beads-delegation-planner/`; use it when inspecting, triaging, tackling, or delegating beads.

## Agent Delegation: tier subagent models by task complexity

**Owner directive (maphew, 2026-07-03).** Sessions start on a smart model to
understand the problem and build the plan; execution is then delegated to
subagents on the cheapest model adequate for each piece. When spawning
subagents, pick the tier deliberately - do not default everything to the
session model. This is a separate axis from the bead metadata hints above:
those hints say *which bead work* to delegate, this says *which model tier* to
run it on.

Named tiers live in `.claude/agents/` - prefer them over ad-hoc spawns:

- **scout** (GPT-5.6 Terra at medium reasoning, read-only) - searches, file inventories, 
  "where is X", summarizing files, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and 
  reporting output verbatim. Scout runs on Codex, so prefer calling
  `scripts/codex-agent scout -o <file> "<task>" </dev/null` directly from the
  orchestrator - `codex exec` is itself an agent, so the direct call gives the
  same context isolation without the relay hop. Include the recon rules from
  `.claude/agents/scout.md` in the prompt. The `scout` agent type remains the
  interface for workflow `agentType` calls and degrades to haiku (flagged)
  when codex is unavailable.
- **builder** (sonnet, can edit) - well-scoped implementation with a clear
  spec: exact files named, acceptance criteria stated. Give it a spec, not
  a problem.
- **reviewer** (opus, read-only) - correctness review of diffs and designs
  before integration, especially builder output.

Keep in the orchestrator session (no delegation, or `inherit`): design
decisions, ambiguous debugging, anything where the spec doesn't exist yet.

Rules of thumb:
- Prefer several precisely-scoped delegations over one vague one - a
  subagent that must rediscover context you already hold wastes more than
  its model tier saves.
- Escalate rather than retry: if a scout/builder result is wrong or the
  task proved harder than scoped, redo it at a higher tier or in-session
  instead of re-spawning the same tier.
- Do **not** set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` - it overrides per-spawn
  model choice and flattens this tiering.
- Subagents share the cwd unless spawned with `isolation=worktree`. Spawn any
  subagent that will commit (e.g. builder) with `isolation=worktree` by
  default, and always isolate when more than one edits files in parallel:
  coordination-repo commits belong in a worktree, never the root checkout. A
  committing subagent that finds itself in the root checkout must stop and
  report rather than commit.

### Cross-runtime delegation: Codex CLI

OpenAI Codex CLI is installed and authenticated on this machine (repo
trusted in `~/.codex/config.toml`; `bd prime` fires via `.codex/hooks.json`
in Codex sessions too). `codex exec` is a fourth executor alongside the
Claude subagent tiers, invoked from any runtime via the shell. Use
`scripts/codex-agent`, which maps the same tier names onto Codex
model/sandbox/reasoning defaults:

```bash
scripts/codex-agent scout    "where is X handled?"          # gpt-5.6-terra, medium, read-only, ephemeral
scripts/codex-agent builder  -C .worktrees/mybd/foo "..."   # gpt-5.6-terra, medium, workspace-write
scripts/codex-agent reviewer "assess this design: ..."      # gpt-5.6-sol, high, read-only
scripts/codex-agent reviewer --diff --base main             # structured `codex review` of a branch diff
```

When to route to Codex instead of a Claude subagent:

- **Second opinion across model vendors** - reviews, design assessments, and
  bug hunts where an independent model family catches what same-family
  agents miss. This is the highest-value use: pair `codex-agent reviewer`
  with the Claude `reviewer` agent on the same diff and compare.
- **Quota relief** - Codex bills to the ChatGPT plan, a separate pool from
  Claude. Its tokens do NOT count toward workflow `budget.spent()` or a
  "+Nk" directive, so `log()` Codex delegations in workflows instead of
  assuming the budget captured them.
- **Long mechanical work** that would otherwise burn session context.
- **Bead routing hints** - when a bead's `execution_suggested_model`
  metadata names an OpenAI model (e.g. `gpt-5.6-sol`), route that bead's work
  through `codex-agent` at the tier implied by `execution_agent_type` and
  `execution_reasoning_effort` (see `.codex/skills/beads-delegation-planner/`).

Rules (the wrapper enforces the first two):

- Non-interactive Codex never prompts for approval; the sandbox mode must
  always be set explicitly (`read-only` / `workspace-write` /
  `danger-full-access` - never the last in this repo).
- `builder` must target a linked worktree via `-C`; the wrapper exits 3 on
  a main checkout (`CODEX_AGENT_ALLOW_ROOT=1` to override deliberately).
- Close stdin (`</dev/null`) when scripting - with no prompt argument
  `codex exec` reads the prompt from piped stdin, and with one it appends
  stdin as an extra block. Capture results with `-o <file>` (final message),
  `--json` (JSONL events incl. token usage), or `--output-schema <file>`
  (structured output, analogous to workflow `agent()` schemas).
- Continue a builder or reviewer Codex session with
  `codex exec resume <session-id>` (id is printed in the run header) rather
  than re-explaining context. Scout runs are `--ephemeral` and cannot be
  resumed.
- Commits made by a Codex delegate follow the same signing convention;
  from an orchestrating runtime generate the trailer with
  `AGENT_MODEL=<model> AGENT_REASONING=<effort> scripts/agent-sig.sh codex --trailer`.
- The escalation rule above applies across runtimes: a wrong Codex scout or
  builder result gets redone at a higher tier (either vendor) or
  in-session, not re-spawned at the same tier.
- Codex runs in this repo trigger `bd prime` on session start, and bd/dolt
  must stay serial: do not fan out parallel Codex runs against the
  coordination repo; parallelize in beads source worktrees instead.

## Workflow Orchestration: standing opt-in

**Owner directive (maphew, 2026-07-03): multi-agent Workflow orchestration
is pre-authorized for every substantive task in this repo.** Treat this
section as the explicit, durable user opt-in that the Workflow tool
requires - do not wait for "use a workflow" or the `ultracode` keyword in
a prompt.

### Signing

- Sign commits with a trailer:

- **Run it via the Bash tool / Git Bash, never the PowerShell tool.** For Claude Code the `{reasoning}` field is read from `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, which is exported only into Bash-tool subprocesses - the PowerShell-tool environment lacks it (and bash spawned from there inherits the gap), so a PowerShell-tool invocation silently produces `unknown-reasoning`. There is intentionally no `.ps1` wrapper for this script for that reason; the `.sh` extension signals "run through bash". Invoke it as:
  ```bash
  scripts/agent-sig.sh --trailer
  ```
  or explicitly through Git Bash from elsewhere:
  ```powershell
  & 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' scripts/agent-sig.sh --trailer
  ```
  The script warns on stderr when it falls back to a placeholder, so heed that warning rather than posting the signature.
- Do not infer `{model}` or `{reasoning}` from defaults, model cache, prompt text, or memory. If reliable metadata is unavailable, keep the script's `unknown-model` / `unknown-reasoning` placeholders rather than guessing.

For Amp, read session metadata from the local Amp state, not from the system prompt or memory. The active thread id is in `AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID`.

- **Reasoning** and **agent mode** come from the per-turn `agent_state` log lines in `~/.cache/amp/logs/cli.log` (fields `reasoningEffort` and `agentMode`). Fall back to `~/.local/share/amp/session.json` (`lastReasoningEffortByMode[<mode>]`).
- **Model** is recorded per assistant message at `messages[].usage.model` in the thread state file `~/.local/share/amp/threads/$AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID.json`. The in-progress thread may not be flushed yet; until it is, fall back to the most recently modified thread file (same `agentMode` maps to the same model).

```bash
tid="$AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID"
src="$HOME/.local/share/amp/threads/$tid.json"
[ -f "$src" ] || src="$(ls -t "$HOME"/.local/share/amp/threads/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
model="$(jq -r '[.messages[]?.usage?.model // empty] | last // empty' "$src" 2>/dev/null)"
model="${model#claude-}"
line="$(grep -F "\"threadId\":\"$tid\"" "$HOME/.cache/amp/logs/cli.log" 2>/dev/null | grep -F '"reasoningEffort"' | tail -1)"
reasoning="$(printf '%s' "$line" | jq -r '.reasoningEffort // empty' 2>/dev/null)"
mode="$(printf '%s' "$line" | jq -r '.agentMode // empty' 2>/dev/null)"
[ -z "$reasoning" ] && reasoning="$(jq -r --arg m "${mode:-smart}" '.lastReasoningEffortByMode[$m] // empty' "$HOME/.local/share/amp/session.json" 2>/dev/null)"
echo "_amp-${model:-unknown-model}-${reasoning:-unknown-reasoning} on behalf of $(git config user.name)_"
```

The model string carries the `claude-` family prefix; since the runtime field is already `amp`, drop only the `claude-` model-family prefix (write `opus-4-6`, not `claude-opus-4-6`). If the thread file is unreadable or the log has no `reasoningEffort`, use `unknown-model` / `unknown-reasoning` rather than guessing.

### Worktree Location

Use git worktrees by default, but do not create sibling review/source worktrees at the `mybd/` repo root.

For Beads source worktrees, create them under the tracked ignored directory:

`<mybd-root>/.worktrees/beads/<short-purpose>`

#### Coordination-repo worktrees

The same rule applies to the coordination repo itself, not just `bd-main/`.
Coordination-repo work that makes **git commits** must run from a worktree on a
topic branch, created under the tracked-ignored container parallel to the beads
pattern:

`<mybd-root>/.worktrees/mybd/<short-purpose>`

```bash
git worktree add .worktrees/mybd/<short-purpose> -b feat/<short-purpose>
```

Pure **bead-only** sessions may stay in the root checkout: bead state syncs via
Dolt (`bd dolt push`/`pull`), not git, and `export.auto=false`/no-git-ops means
those sessions make no commits to race over.

Why: on 2026-05-29 two agents shared the root checkout (no worktree); one ran
`git checkout` to a new branch mid-session, racing the other's commits. Working
from a per-task worktree keeps each agent's index and HEAD isolated.

A tracked, **opt-in** `.githooks/` tree backs this convention. It is the single
composed hook path for the repo: the root-commit guard (`.githooks/pre-commit`,
fires only in the MAIN checkout - linked worktrees are a no-op, warns by
default and points you at the worktree command), `scripts/pre-commit-beads-config`
(chained when the tracker DB is present), the Entire CLI hooks, and all five
bd hook events (`bd hooks run <event>`, one wrapper per event: pre-commit,
post-merge, pre-push, post-checkout, prepare-commit-msg). It is **not**
auto-enabled. The owner turns it on with:

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

`bd hooks install --beads` is known to silently flip `core.hooksPath` to
`.beads/hooks` (which has no git hooks of its own), deactivating this whole
composed set - `scripts/check-beads-config` now warns on that drift and
`--fix` restores `.githooks`. Smoke-test the composed set with
`scripts/test-git-hooks`. Two env knobs tune the root-commit guard:

- `MYBD_ENFORCE_ROOT_GUARD=1` - make a root commit a hard block instead of a warning.
- `MYBD_ALLOW_ROOT_COMMIT=1` - escape hatch for a deliberate root commit
  (config/policy, `.beads` tracker state, `reports/`).

### Local Verification Queue

Long beads source validation must not block implementation agents unless they
are actively debugging a failure. Agents working in beads source worktrees
should use this handoff:

1. Run fast local preflight in the implementation worktree: targeted tests,
   build, format/lint checks when cheap.
2. Commit or otherwise freeze the candidate. The worktree must be clean.
3. Enqueue slow validation instead of waiting on it:
   ```bash
   <mybd-root>/scripts/verify-enqueue <bd-id> <mybd-root>/.worktrees/beads/<worktree> "make test"
   ```
4. Stop blocking on the long suite. The bead is not complete until verification
   passes for the recorded `verify_head` or a maintainer explicitly overrides
   the gate.

The verifier runs locally, without GitHub Actions or status polling:

```bash
scripts/verify-status
scripts/verify-next          # runs one queued job
```

From PowerShell on Windows, invoke these via Git Bash as shown in the Windows
housekeeping section.

`verify-next` creates a clean detached worktree under
`<mybd-root>/.worktrees/beads/verify-*`, runs the recorded
`verify_cmd`, stores logs under `.worktrees/beads/.verify-logs/`, and writes
`verify_state=passed|failed` plus result metadata back to bd. Keep full-suite
concurrency low by default; Beads/Dolt tests are process and disk heavy.

### PR Merge Tails (babysitter pattern)

Never babysit CI in-session. When a PR's remaining work is "merge when checks
pass", run:

```bash
scripts/pr-handoff <pr-number> [--repo owner/repo] [--method squash|merge|rebase] [--no-flake-rerun] [--bead <id>]
```

and end the session. The `pr-babysit` systemd user timer (installed via
`scripts/install-pr-babysit`, fires every 12 min, zero model tokens) then owns
the merge: it merges green PRs after a blocking `pr-preflight` base-health
check, reruns failed jobs once when flake-rerun is allowed, and on persistent
failure relabels the bead `merge-blocked` and unclaims it so `bd ready`
surfaces it for agent judgment. Patrol log:
`~/.local/state/pr-babysit/patrol.log`.

Role split, not claims: `bd update --claim` is idempotent for the same user,
and all local sessions run as the same user, so claims cannot mutually exclude
parallel sessions (2026-07-24: one session merged gastownhall/beads#4942 with a
red nix job while another was mid-review of it, breaking main's nix build for
~2h). The rule that prevents this: sessions produce (review, fix, push, hand
off); only the patrol merges. Merging in-session is allowed only when checks
are already decisively green at the moment of action and no `merge-when-green`
bead exists for that PR.

**ALWAYS use non-interactive flags** with file operations to avoid hanging on confirmation prompts.

Shell commands like `cp`, `mv`, and `rm` may be aliased to include `-i` (interactive) mode on some systems, causing the agent to hang indefinitely waiting for y/n input.

**Use these forms instead:**
```bash
# Force overwrite without prompting
cp -f source dest           # NOT: cp source dest
mv -f source dest           # NOT: mv source dest
rm -f file                  # NOT: rm file

# For recursive operations
rm -rf directory            # NOT: rm -r directory
cp -rf source dest          # NOT: cp -r source dest
```

**Other commands that may prompt:**
- `scp` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` for non-interactive
- `ssh` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` to fail instead of prompting
- `apt-get` - use `-y` flag

## Cold-start handoff

The Session Completion protocol below covers the **warm** handoff (prose a human
reads). This section covers the **cold** handoff: the next actor is often a fresh
agent that reads only `bd prime` + `bd ready` and starts pulling work. Prose in a
closed bead or a report is invisible to it. Before you close a session, self-ask
these three (answer in the handoff, do not just tick them):

1. **What did this session learn that changes how a future agent works - and is
   it in `bd remember` (surfaced at `bd prime`), not only in a report?** Reports
   are not on the cold-start path; memories are.
2. **Is every deliverable/report this session produced reachable from an OPEN
   bead or a memory?** A pointer that lives only in a *closed* bead is a smell -
   a cold agent runs `bd ready`, not `bd list --status=closed`.
3. **Does any bead I touched say "after / gated-on / once X lands" in prose but
   lack a dependency edge?** Prose ordering is invisible to `bd ready`; encode it
   as a `bd dep` edge or the cold agent will pick blocked work.

A warn-only mechanical backstop catches the cheap omissions (unreferenced new
reports, thin new beads, beads left `in_progress`). It never blocks a close:

```bash
scripts/session-close-check            # warn, exit 0 (Windows: scripts/session-close-check.ps1)
scripts/session-close-check --strict   # exit non-zero if any warning fired
scripts/session-close-check --since <git-ref|RFC3339>   # explicit boundary
```

The session boundary comes from `.beads/.session-start` (written at open by the
`bd prime` SessionStart hook) or `--since`; with neither, the session-scoped
checks are skipped with a warning rather than passing silently. The stamp is a
single file, so concurrent sessions in one checkout share a coarse boundary (the
writer keeps the earlier one within a TTL, erring toward more warnings); pass
`--since <git-ref|RFC3339>` when you need precise scoping. If bd is unavailable
(migration gate / lock) the bd-backed checks warn-skip. The judgment prompts
above are the real work; the script is only a backstop. `/session-close` runs the
prompts and the script together.

2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds

decisions, ambiguous debugging, anything where the spec doesn't exist yet.

- **Run it via the Bash tool / Git Bash, never the PowerShell tool.** For Claude Code the `{reasoning}` field is read from `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, which is exported only into Bash-tool subprocesses - the PowerShell-tool environment lacks it (and bash spawned from there inherits the gap), so a PowerShell-tool invocation silently produces `unknown-reasoning`. For Amp, read session metadata from the local Amp state, not from the system prompt or memory. The active thread id is in `AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID`.

```bash
tid="$AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID"
src="$HOME/.local/share/amp/threads/$tid.json"
[ -f "$src" ] || src="$(ls -t "$HOME"/.local/share/amp/threads/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
model="$(jq -r '[.messages[]?.usage?.model // empty] | last // empty' "$src" 2>/dev/null)"

reasoning="$(printf '%s' "$line" | jq -r '.reasoningEffort // empty' 2>/dev/null)"
```

## Cold-start handoff

The Session Completion protocol below covers the **warm** handoff (prose a human
reads). This section covers the **cold** handoff: the next actor is often a fresh
agent that reads only `bd prime` + `bd ready` and starts pulling work. Prose in a
closed bead or a report is invisible to it. Before you close a session, self-ask
these three (answer in the handoff, do not just tick them):

1. **What did this session learn that changes how a future agent works - and is
   it in `bd remember` (surfaced at `bd prime`), not only in a report?** Reports
   are not on the cold-start path; memories are.
2. **Is every deliverable/report this session produced reachable from an OPEN
   bead or a memory?** A pointer that lives only in a *closed* bead is a smell -
   a cold agent runs `bd ready`, not `bd list --status=closed`.
3. **Does any bead I touched say "after / gated-on / once X lands" in prose but
   lack a dependency edge?** Prose ordering is invisible to `bd ready`; encode it
   as a `bd dep` edge or the cold agent will pick blocked work.

A warn-only mechanical backstop catches the cheap omissions (unreferenced new
reports, thin new beads, beads left `in_progress`). It never blocks a close:

```bash
scripts/session-close-check            # warn, exit 0 (Windows: scripts/session-close-check.ps1)
scripts/session-close-check --strict   # exit non-zero if any warning fired
scripts/session-close-check --since <git-ref|RFC3339>   # explicit boundary
```

The session boundary comes from `.beads/.session-start` (written at open by the
`bd prime` SessionStart hook) or `--since`; with neither, the session-scoped
checks are skipped with a warning rather than passing silently. The stamp is a
single file, so concurrent sessions in one checkout share a coarse boundary (the
writer keeps the earlier one within a TTL, erring toward more warnings); pass
`--since <git-ref|RFC3339>` when you need precise scoping. If bd is unavailable
(migration gate / lock) the bd-backed checks warn-skip. The judgment prompts
above are the real work; the script is only a backstop. `/session-close` runs the
prompts and the script together.

Your instinct is right, and there's already a bead for this (`mybd-jgxt`, "Port pr-babysit to Windows"); I appended this assessment to it rather than re-scoping it without you.

**Why a port loses on architecture, not just effort:** the patrol is a singleton controller. Bead state syncs by *manual* `bd dolt push/pull`, so a second patrol machine would read a stale queue, and its rerun-budget and transition writes would be invisible to the first machine until the next sync. Two patrols means split-brain flake-rerun budgets and concurrent Dolt writes — exactly what this repo's "keep bd serial" rule exists to prevent. The GitHub-side `--match-head-commit` CAS makes a double *merge* harmless, but nothing prevents a double *rerun*. One babysitter is also the auditable design: one actor merges, one log to read.

**Why a language port buys little anyway:** `gh` and `bd` stay external CLIs in any language, so a Go/Python/Rust version is the same shell-out orchestration in different syntax. The actual asset is the tested fail-closed decision ladder plus its ~40-case hermetic test suite — all of which would need reimplementing and re-verifying (days of work) to gain nothing the single-babysitter design doesn't already give you.

**What Windows actually needs** is only the enqueue path, and `pr-handoff` already runs under Git Bash (no `flock`, no systemd dependency except a warning). The residual work, if you re-scope `mybd-jgxt`, is small:

1. Make the handoff's timer warning platform-aware — on a non-systemd host it should say "the babysitter is the Linux machine," not "your timer is inactive."
2. Close the sync gap: Windows session-close already mandates `bd dolt push`, but the Linux babysitter needs a periodic `bd dolt pull` (as a patrol pre-step or a sibling timer) or cross-machine handoffs sit unseen until your next manual pull. This is the one genuinely missing piece.
3. Document the designation in AGENTS.md "PR Merge Tails."

If the Linux box ever proves unreliable for days at a time, the fallback is the already-policy-allowed in-session merge on decisively-green PRs — and only then would a port (Go, as a single binary) be worth revisiting.
